fa96b4fd9f.why: Old tell fixed: the two 'fell to 8' choices are now decided by the ecology, not a count. Nautilus confirms the sea stars ate barnacles, chitons, limpets, snails and mussels, and that the two limpet and two chiton species left the cleared plot by June 1964 (so the limpet-grazing choice is truly wrong); 15 to 8 within a year is in SciAm, Scitable and Grokipedia. Easy arithmetic. It does not re-ask the T1 one-step removal: it keys the opposite result. No other unit asks Paine.

2593fea18f.why: Wording fix only ('thinned out' in all four choices), and it reads clearly. Facts unchanged and checked before; the debate stays attributed and hedged. No overlap with the T2 lynx-hare cycle or any other unit.

5d81c07557.why: The T1 one-step overlap is fixed: the stem no longer gives the otter-urchin link. UCSC (Estes 1998) confirms first attacks seen in 1991, about 25 percent a year otter decline, the stable Clam Lagoon, and kelp densities down by a factor of 12 since the otters began to disappear. The fish and seal-dropping choices are live rival chains (the whales usually eat seals) and wrong. The context's 'more hunting by the whales' fixes the old error. Nothing else in the bank asks otters, urchins or kelp.

a93f48b7c3.why: Context fix verified: keelback snakes and meat ants do take toads, so 'that few native animals can safely eat' is true where 'no natural enemies' was not. Stem, choices and key unchanged and sourced (Doody et al. 2015: monitors down near 50 percent, fledging 55 to 81 percent). The judge's low lone-gain tell remains but was rated acceptable.

3e5c758fab.why: Context fix verified against Pedler et al. 2016: dusky hopping mouse about five-fold, plains mouse three- to four-fold, mulgara far more, spinifex hopping mouse 1.5 to 2 times, so 'most of them several times as much' is true. Two of the four are hopping mice. Rest unchanged and sourced.

f1671ec4e6.why: New key matches Leahy et al. 2015 (Wildlife Research): high-intensity, low-intensity patchy and unburnt treatments; pale field rat and western chestnut mouse trapped; 38 pale field rats radio-tracked; both fell after fire, most after the hot burn; of the tested causes direct fire deaths, starvation, poorer breeding and emigration were not supported and predation was; cats and snakes caught in the act. The stem names no predator and all four choices are causes the study tested, so the old 'open ground' tell is gone. The 12 km trips and 70 against 17 percent in the context match McGregor's work. Scope names fire; no overlap elsewhere.

7fd439d92c.why: The uncertain 3 parts per trillion water figure is gone, and 'more than six hundred times' (0.04 to 25) is right and easy to check. The 0.5 / 2 / 25 chain is the much-quoted rounding of Woodwell's results, not single table values. The paper's own range runs from 0.04 ppm in plankton to 75 ppm in a gull, with fish-eating birds at about 3 to 25, and 'about' hedges each figure. The key (storage from many meals) and the three wrong choices are sound. The T3 DDT question is about resistance in flies, a different fact.

11870f3841.why: The date-recall tell is fixed: the choices are now four shapes of the record. Ratcliffe's index was steady for over 125 years, then fell 16 percent from 1947, so the key is true and the gradual, no-thinning and random choices are wrong. Wikipedia (David Peakall) confirms the industry's 'too rapidly' claim and DDE in 1946 British eggs. The stem never names DDT, so the key needs the story.
